source.title: Stochastic Weight Averaging Revisited
source.authors: Hao Guo; Ji-Yong Jin; B. Liu

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, though some figure results are only described qualitatively or shown as figures.
record.tranche_reason: The study directly tests how weight averaging and learning-rate schedules affect generalization and whether wider optima accompany improved test performance. It finds that SWA does not always yield better generalization or wider optima, with outcomes depending on convergence and momentum.
record.gate_note: The paper studies stochastic weight averaging (SWA), not arbitrary-label memorization or the listed version claims directly. Its CIFAR, ImageNet, graph, and text results bear on V7's sharpness/generalization association and provide some related generalization findings. The cited literature on sharpness and generalization is not counted as the paper's own result.
record.test_reason: The study tests explanations of stochastic weight averaging, but none of V1–V8 directly. Its closest results concern unscaled loss profiles along lines connecting solutions and test accuracy. These do not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or its association with training–test gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors attribute SWA's behavior to learning-rate scheduling that discovers global loss-landscape structures and averaging that exploits them while reducing variance. They report that SWA need not improve accuracy or find wider optima. PSWA improves early-training performance, while its final outputs are indistinguishable from SGD's; the proposed geometric explanation lacks theoretical support.
record.recipe_differences: The study investigates SWA, DSWA, and PSWA behavior, rather than measuring magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or comparing generalization measures as in V7.
record.method_sensitivity: Results depend on whether preceding SGD converged and whether momentum was removed; the authors also report varying outcomes across datasets and model settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Without momentum, SWA gives equal or slightly lower test accuracy than its SGD baseline in the toy CNN and PreResNet-164 experiments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight averaging does not invariably improve held-out accuracy; its benefit depends on the training conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: DSWA/TSWA yield flatter connecting-line profiles and better test accuracy after non-converged SGD, but fail to find flatter optima after converged SGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The performance and directional-flatness benefits of repeated weight averaging depend on preceding SGD convergence.

record.problems: The paper says its findings lack theoretical support and may not hold for all DNN tasks. Several image ablation results are presented as figures without exact numeric values. The flatness comparisons do not test the magnitude-aware perturbation measure in V7.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant result rows beyond those extracted. Figures 1, 2, and 7 report test-accuracy comparisons for SWA samples, SWA, and SGD, but do not measure the flatness/generalization relation named by V7; exact figure values are unavailable in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out performance.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets. Adam versus SWA comparisons do not isolate this contrast.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Controlled dropout comparisons and dropout–augmentation interactions.

Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with training–test gaps among similarly fitted networks, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. Connecting-line loss profiles do not establish these quantities.
Removal of highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Failure of an averaging method to produce wider optima does not itself challenge a correlation between sharpness and generalization. All row states are cannot_determine with respect to the supplied claim versions, rather than judgments about whether the reported SWA comparisons occurred.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-network comparison.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD generalization under tuning.
Large versus small batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures were not tested; the paper compares local flatness and generalization qualitatively in selected cases.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: toy CNN model
rows.operation_detail: Train SGD, then replace last L iterations with SWA without momentum.
rows.note: Authors state this indicates SWA does not lead to wider optima in this case.
rows.check: The accuracy values match the text, but lower SWA accuracy alone establishes neither sharpness nor its relationship with the generalization gap. 'Reversed' is unsupported for V7.

rows.subject: toy CNN model
rows.operation_detail: Replace last L iterations of SGD with SWA without momentum.
rows.note: The stated values do not show an improvement.
rows.check: Equal test accuracy does not establish the absence of V7's sharpness–gap association. No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement is reported.

rows.subject: PreResNet-164
rows.operation_detail: Run SWA after SGD converges; close momentum and L2-based weight regularization.
rows.note: Authors state the SWA result is smaller than the converged SGD result.
rows.check: The reported accuracies match the text, but this is an SWA performance comparison without a sharpness measurement or measured generalization-gap association.
